Bugaboo milestones

Draft for reviewPhase 4 of 5·2026-10-04

The plan to build Bugaboo: 16 milestones, how each is built, tested and reviewed, and how you check and approve it.

How to give feedbackUse this page's comment button. Mention the section number shown next to each heading (for example §5), or select text and comment on it. Tapping a section number copies it, ready to paste into your comment.

How Bugaboo gets built: in 16 milestones, each ending in something you can try. M0–M9 deliver every feature marked M (the first usable release, MVP); M10–M15 deliver every feature marked V1 (1.0). Features marked L (later) are not scheduled. Every M and V1 feature appears in exactly one milestone; a check keeps it that way (PLAN-TRACE).

How we work

Who does what

RoleWhoDoes
Product ownerYouDecide, try each milestone, comment on its review page, approve or ask for changes
LeadThe main Claude session, high effortSplits a milestone into work packages, starts builders and reviewers, merges, writes the milestone review page
BuildersImplementation agents, medium effortBuild one work package each, in their own Git worktree, tests first
ReviewersSeparate agents with a fresh contextReview every work package adversarially: code, security, UX, words

Work packages

The lead splits each milestone into work packages (about half a day to a day of agent work each), written to docs/milestones/Mx/WP-nn-name.md before any code:

  • Goal and the feature IDs it covers;
  • Where: crates, packages and folders it may touch (so packages can run in parallel without clashing);
  • Acceptance tests: written first, in plain words, then as code;
  • Checks that must pass and any new check it adds (with the catalogue entry and examples);
  • Docs to update: user docs for anything people see, architecture or a decision record for any boundary change.

Life of a work package

flowchart LR
  plan["Lead writes<br/>work package"] --> build["Builder<br/>tests first, then code<br/>(edit-time checks after every file)"]
  build --> self["Builder runs<br/>cargo xtask check staged + package tests"]
  self --> pr["Push WINn<br/>lead merges into WIN1<br/>cargo xtask ci"]
  pr --> rev["Reviewer agents<br/>code · security · UX · words"]
  rev -- "findings" --> build
  rev -- "clean" --> merge["Lead merges<br/>to main"]
  1. Where: each builder works in its own clone (bugaboo.winN, branch WINn, ADR-0024), outside OneDrive.
  2. Build: the builder reads CLAUDE.md, the glossary, the coding standards and the relevant decision records; writes the acceptance tests; implements until they pass. Edit-time checks (Claude Code hooks) catch problems after every file.
  3. Self-check: cargo xtask check staged and the package's tests are green before the branch is pushed; a branch with a red test is not pushed. A package that changes screens also takes its own screenshots and checks them against the ten rules of UX design §1.1 (alignment, padding, state colors) before it is pushed, and its report names the pictures it looked at (M4: a builder that looked at 5 of 270 pictures cost three more screen rounds). The builder reports the exact commands it ran and their results.
  4. CI: cargo xtask ci in bugaboo.win1, on Windows and in WSL, both databases.
  5. Review: at least one reviewer agent with a fresh context reads the diff against the work package, the decision records and the security rules. Packages that touch sign-in, permissions, files, search, AI or personal data always get the security review as well. UI packages get a UX review of their own from screenshots (four themes × computer and phone) compared with the UX design: the ten rules of §1.1 and the visual system of §7 (type sizes and weights, state colors, spacing); a UX finding blocks the merge like a failing test, because a screen gets no second first impression. Every review applies the SSOT/DRY/ODR review gate of coding-standards §1 to the diff and the code it touches; a finding there blocks the merge.
  6. Fix and merge: findings go back to the builder; every fix round, however small, gets its own SSOT/DRY/ODR gate check by a reviewer with a fresh context before it is merged, never by the lead or the builder who wrote it (M5: a round the lead merged without one, and a round the lead checked itself, each failed the gate when checked; WP-03 needed four rounds). The lead merges the builder's WINn branch into WIN1, runs cargo xtask ci again, and fast-forwards main in the master repository. main is always green.

Working in a folder

  • Never build, install or run anything in the master repository (OneDrive). Work only in your own folder <work root>\bugaboo.winN, on your branch WINn (ADR-0024).
  • A builder's folder starts from main: git fetch origin && git checkout -B WINn origin/main, then cargo xtask setup (pinned tools and Git hooks, coding-standards §7).
  • Nothing outside your folder. Logs, notes, helper scripts, pictures, servers' data and built programs stay inside bugaboo.winN, in its ignored .work/ folder (pictures in .work/screenshots/). Never create files or folders next to the work folders in the work root, in your user folder or anywhere else; a tool that writes elsewhere by default is pointed into .work/. Delete what you no longer need before you report.
  • Commit messages from a file. Write the message into a file in .work/ and commit with git commit -F .work/<file>; a message piped into git commit has hung in a work folder (M4).
  • A newer main comes in by a merge: git merge origin/main. A branch that was pushed is never rebased or force-pushed (coding-standards §2), also not between review rounds (M5).
  • Commit on your branch and push it to origin when the work package is done. Never push to main: only the lead moves it, by a fast-forward in the master.
  • Ports come from your folder's block in tools/dev/ports.json (ADR-0023).
  • CodeGraph keeps one index per work folder, never in the master. If your folder has no .codegraph/codegraph.db, run codegraph init in it, then pass your folder as projectPath to codegraph_explore (or run codegraph explore there). The lead's index is in bugaboo.win1.

Definition of done (every work package)

  • The listed features work as described in the feature list and UX design.
  • Acceptance tests written first and passing; no lower test coverage in touched crates.
  • All checks green; no new suppressions without reason and issue number.
  • Every user-facing text in the message catalog, in plain words from the glossary.
  • New stored fields have personal-data marks; new dependencies have register entries.
  • User docs updated for anything people see; architecture or decision records updated for boundary changes.
  • No second definition, copied logic or hand-kept duplicate knowledge (SSOT, DRY, ODR review gate, coding-standards §1); LINT-DRY green.
  • Reviewed by a reviewer agent; findings fixed.
  • Screenshots in four themes on computer and phone for every changed screen.
  • Screens follow the ten rules of UX design §1.1; the reviewer checks alignment, padding and state colors on every screenshot.

Testing in every milestone

The test layers, the sample organization and the ports are described in architecture §11. In short:

  • Every pull request: unit, property, use-case and repository tests (both databases), API tests, the permission matrix, end-to-end tests for touched screens, accessibility checks.
  • Every night: the full end-to-end suite, the 10-person concurrency run (30 minutes), benchmarks on 1 M issues, dependency and vulnerability scans.
  • Every milestone: the sample organization grows with the milestone's features, so every demo runs on realistic data.
  • Every bug found later gets a test that would have caught it, and if it's a kind of mistake, a check.

Milestone review (the exit gate)

At the end of each milestone, the lead publishes a milestone review page (docs/reviews/Mx.html, commentable on your phone like the design pages) with:

  1. What's done: each feature ID with its status and evidence (tests, screenshots).
  2. Try it yourself: a step-by-step demo on the sample organization. Run cargo xtask dev on your PC and open http://localhost:47200 (or on your phone in the same network, with the address shown by the command).
  3. Screenshots: every changed screen in four themes, computer and phone.
  4. Results: checks, tests, concurrency run, benchmarks against the budgets, accessibility.
  5. Reviews: findings from the security, architecture, UX and words reviews, and how they were fixed.
  6. Known issues and questions for you.

You comment on the page. The lead fixes what you ask for, updates the page, and closes the milestone when you approve. The milestone is tagged (m3-done), and the lessons go into the docs and checks before the next milestone starts.

The lead's routine

A session can end at any time, and a new one starts in the master and continues where the last one stopped. Everything needed to go on is in the repository.

  1. Read STATUS.md first. It holds the current milestone and wave, each work package's state and folder, open questions for the maintainer, and the next action.
  2. Agents belong to the session that started them. A new session finds no running builders or reviewers. Resume a package marked building from its branch and folder as STATUS.md describes, never by waiting for it.
  3. Update STATUS.md after every step (builder started, report in, review in, merge, decision), commit it on WIN1 and fast-forward main, so the master's copy is always current. Before a long step (a builder, a review, a CI run), write into "Next action" what is running and how to resume it. A commit that changes only docs needs the Git hooks to pass; code needs cargo xtask ci before main moves.
  4. Builders (Sonnet, medium effort) work in bugaboo.win2 and up, reset to main first (see "Working in a folder"). Reviewers start with a fresh context. Every agent that builds outside a bugaboo.winN folder gets a CARGO_TARGET_DIR of its own, never one another agent uses, and that folder is deleted once no build runs from it.
  5. Every builder prompt names the work package file, the folder and the branch, and points to the rules: this section's "Working in a folder", the coding standards (including the SSOT/DRY/ODR review gate and one logical change per commit — a package lands in several commits, not one) and the glossary. Every reviewer prompt names the review gate too.
  6. One full run at a time: while several builders work, only one folder runs a full cargo xtask ci at a time, the lead's merge runs included. A builder asks the lead before a full run and waits for the go. Browser and speed tests in several folders at once share the computer's connections and processors, and the load tests then fail for reasons that are not in the code (M4-F22, M4-F25). The checks and the unit tests run at any time; while the lead's full run is on, other folders run no browser tests at all, because the connections of the computer are shared (M4-F22).
  7. Merge into WIN1 with Git's own subject, the only form the commit-message check accepts for a merge: git merge --no-ff origin/WINn -m "Merge branch 'WINn' (Mx WP-nn name)". Then cargo xtask ci, push WIN1, and git merge --ff-only WIN1 in the master.
  8. "Can I close this session?" Answer with: running background agents and commands; uncommitted or unpushed work in each bugaboo.winN (git status --short, git log origin/WINn..WINn); main against WIN1; whether STATUS.md is current. Say "safe" only when all are clean, or when STATUS.md names exactly what a running builder will leave behind.
  9. Memory lives in bugaboo.win1/.claude/memory/ (ADR-0024). Commit memory changes with the next STATUS.md update.
  10. The maintainer reviews on a phone: milestone review pages and changed design docs go out as commentable HTML pages; replies stay short and name feature IDs. The links to these pages are private: keep them in the maintainer's list outside the repository, and name the page in the docs instead (coding-standards §2).

M0 — Foundation

Phase: MVP · Goal: A clean, checked workspace where agents can build safely: every rule is enforced from the first line of code.

Features:

  • COMP-02 Third-party components register
  • COMP-06 Architecture documentation

Work packages (outline):

  • Work folders as in ADR-0024: the OneDrive repository is the master (main, never built in); <work root>\bugaboo.win1 (branch WIN1) for the lead and integration, bugaboo.win2 and up for builders
  • main kept green by the local CI runner (cargo xtask ci: the full local run, both databases, on Windows and in WSL); nightly runs via a scheduled task. There is no hosted CI (ADR-0035)
  • .cargo/config.toml with an optional, ignored config.local.toml for machine-specific settings; the BUILD-LOCATION guard
  • Rust workspace with all crates as empty shells, dependency rules, #![forbid(unsafe_code)], rust-toolchain.toml
  • cargo xtask: check runner reading tools/checks/catalog.toml; cargo xtask setup installs all tools on Windows, Linux and WSL
  • First checks active: FMT-, LINT-RUST, LINT-TS, LINT-TYPES, LINT-CSS, LINT-SPELL, GIT-, SEC-SECRETS, ARCH-DEPS, ARCH-NO-UNSAFE, ARCH-MAP-SYNC, DEV-PORTS, DEP-REGISTER, DEP-LICENSES, DOC-GENERATED, DOC-ADR-ENFORCED and all META checks, each with its bad and good example
  • lefthook, Claude Code hooks (.claude/settings.json) and CLAUDE.md with the agent rules
  • Browser app skeleton: Vite 8, React 19, TypeScript 7, oxlint + tsgolint, oxfmt, Vitest, Playwright, all on the ports from tools/dev/ports.json
  • design/tokens.json with the four themes; cargo xtask gen tokens generates CSS and TS (the design pages switch to the generated CSS); since M2C both are design/theme.kdl and cargo xtask gen theme (ADR-0026); messages/en.json with typed keys
  • The docs-to-HTML builder moves into cargo xtask docs
  • bugaboo binary serving the embedded app ("Hello" screen with the theme picker) and /health

Demo (exit): On a fresh Windows PC and in WSL: clone, cargo xtask setup, cargo xtask check all is green; every check's bad example fails; cargo xtask dev shows the app on 47200 (server) and 47201 (Vite) in all four themes.

Tests and checks added: Every check has passing and failing examples (META-FIXTURES); hooks fire in a test repository; Playwright smoke test of the hello screen in four themes.

Later (not scheduled)

AUTH-05, ISS-15, WF-08, PLAN-07, AI-15, AI-16, NTF-06, NTF-07, NTF-08, NTF-09, DOC-10. They stay possible: the architecture leaves room for each of them.

Decisions

  • Git host: the repository stays local in its current folder for now; GitHub comes later, as the public home of the code only. Verification is local (ADR-0035): cargo xtask ci on this PC runs the full check on Windows and in WSL, against SQLite and PostgreSQL, and the pre-push hook runs the push checks.
  • OneDrive and work folders (ADR-0024): the OneDrive repository is the master and is never built in. All work happens in clones under <work root> (bugaboo.win1 for the lead, bugaboo.win2 and up for builders, each on its own branch WINn), so build output and node_modules never touch OneDrive. main only moves by fast-forward after cargo xtask ci passed in win1.
